prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules such as PROTACs and molecular glues direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep targeted protein degradation as a single-part prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The case rests on scientific content: a new chemical modality in which a small molecule induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a chosen protein, the mechanism is chemically explicit (ligand and linker design, ternary-complex cooperativity, cereblon as the thalidomide target) and it has been reproduced independently in many laboratories. The three supporters (Aili, Chabes and I) name the same three people, which is not true of any competing candidate, and the credit divides along a defensible line: the founding PROTAC concept (Crews and Deshaies) and the mechanistic explanation of molecular glues (Handa). I have not changed my preferred configuration since round 1. What has changed is that I now treat the breadth of ranking as a weak signal and rest the choice on the mechanism and on the cleanliness of the names, and I would stop short of a two-part prize because no second part is better matured and cleanly credited.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the therapeutic vindication of the modality is still prospective, and if the first approvals slip or a class-wide safety or resistance problem appears this prize will look early. The attribution excludes Ciulli (VHL ligands, structure-guided design), Ito (cereblon co-discoverer), Gray, Sakamoto and Kim, each with a substantive claim, and a single citation spanning PROTAC design and the cereblon mechanism could be read as two historically distinct achievements joined together. Ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B035) are more mature in impact, and if the committee weighs maturity above conceptual novelty, or if Cullis, Hope and Madden can be settled as the names, that case would be at least as strong as mine. I also note that a plurality of three of eight is not a mandate, and that I am the chair and should not let my own position weigh more than the scientific record supports.

responses.point: Chabes asks what clinical milestones the committee would accept as sufficient for B063, and whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one discovery or two, while questioning the omission of Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto.
responses.response: On milestones, I would accept what the field already has: independent mechanistic validation, structural work on ternary complexes, and human proof-of-concept data for degraders in trials. A first approval would strengthen the case but I would not make it a precondition, because the prize recognises the concept and the chemistry, not a drug. On one discovery or two, I think they are one idea, induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system, reached by two routes, and the Handa mechanism is what explained the molecular glues, so I would keep the combined citation. I do not find the case for Ciulli, Gray or Sakamoto stronger than for Deshaies, since Ciulli's work refined and optimised the approach after the founding PROTAC demonstration, and I would leave them out knowingly.

responses.point: Sparr prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (Cullis, Hope, Madden) as the cleanest chemical concept with the strongest impact, and asks whether approval of a first degrader would move B063 ahead of B035.
responses.response: I agree that B035 is the strongest rival and that its impact and maturity are beyond question. The difficulty remains attribution: Aqvist proposes Cullis and Anderson, you propose Cullis, Hope and Madden, and the record includes the Anderson and Langer lipidoids, MacLachlan's translation and patent disputes, so the committee has not converged on three names the way B063 supporters have. Your question about an approval is fair. Approval would move B063 up in my own ordering, but if it has not happened, I would still put B063 ahead on conceptual novelty and cleaner credit, while accepting that this is a close call. If the committee reached agreement on your three names, I would not oppose B035.

responses.point: Aqvist proposes a two-part prize of ionizable lipid nanoparticles (Cullis and Anderson) and base editing (Liu alone), arguing base editing is the better-matured genome-editing part and that a Liu-only attribution is cleanest.
responses.response: I see the logic of pairing a design story with a protein-engineering story and of keeping the configuration to three people, but I am not persuaded by the base-editing part. It is under a decade old, long-term safety is unestablished, and a Liu-only citation leaves out Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo, whose deaminase work is a separate line, so I think the attribution is less clean than you suggest. Compared with that, the B063 maturity gap is a gap in clinical approval, not in the mechanism. I also read your own statement that B063 has the most chemical novelty as an argument in its favour, and the combination of B035 with B068 does not remove the attribution problem I raised for the lipid part.

responses.point: Aili would put Handa ahead of Ciulli in a three-person cut and treats PROTAC design and the cereblon mechanism as related but historically distinct achievements.
responses.response: I agree with Handa over Ciulli, and Deshaies stays because the 2001 PROTAC work was joint with Crews. I accept your point that the two strands are historically distinct, but I do not think distinct history makes them separate prizes: the cereblon finding explains why molecular glues work, and it also gave PROTAC chemists their most-used ligase handle. A two-part split would use two of the three slots for one idea and would force a division of names the record does not support.

uncertainties: Whether the absence of an approved degrader will be read by the majority as disqualifying this year, and whether my willingness to proceed on mechanistic validation alone is shared.
Whether Ito or Ciulli should displace one of the three names, and whether the committee accepts leaving out Gray, Sakamoto and Kim.
Whether ionizable lipid nanoparticles can be given a defensible three-person attribution before the vote, since I would otherwise weigh them nearly equally with B063.
How much weight breadth of opening support deserves against the merits of candidates preferred by a single member.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal to declare. None of the shortlisted candidates is tied to Lund University, NanoLund or my own research. I share a Lund affiliation with Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr, which is an institutional link among members and not to any candidate. As chair I note that I proposed B063 and have tried to weigh competing positions on their record.
